title: Labels + due-date combo
description: Probes the combined label-creation + label-application + due-date-setting flow across several tasks at once -- a common realistic ask that touches three different concepts in one request. REVERTED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 T1, correcting PR #179's re-baseline): the honest optimum WAS create-project (1) + create-label (1, or let bulk-create's per-task `labels` title-resolve/get-or-create it) + bulk-create 5 tasks each carrying `labels: ["{{prefix}}urgent"]` and `dueDate` set to next Friday in the same call (1) = 3, because PR #179 reached 1 call only by routing through vikunja_projects' setup-kanban composite with a fabricated placeholder column (["{{prefix}}Tasks"]) that nothing in the prompt asked for -- see docs/BATTLE-TESTING.md's 'Re-baselining optimalCallCount' policy (rule 3) for the full history and why that route was never creditable. RE-BASELINED AGAIN 2026-07-27 (issue #185), for a genuinely different reason than PR #179's mistake: `setup-kanban`'s `columns` argument is now OPTIONAL (issue #185) -- calling it with a `title` and a `tasks` array but NO `columns` at all creates the project and its tasks in one call while resolving/creating/touching ZERO Kanban view or bucket (verified: `kanban-setup.ts`'s columns-less path never calls `resolveKanbanView`). That is not the placeholder-column trick reverted above -- no Kanban structure is fabricated, board or otherwise, so rule 3's 'requires NO structure, view, board, column, or other state the prompt did not ask for' test is satisfied for the first time on this scenario. The prompt itself never asks for or implies a Kanban board, and this route creates none. `setup-kanban` is simply the tool's name; its columns-less form is a plain project+tasks composite, exactly what this scenario's end state is. New optimum: setup-kanban with `title`, and `tasks: [{title, labels: ["{{prefix}}urgent"], dueDate: <next Friday>}, ...]` x5, no `columns` (1).
promptTemplate: Create a project called "{{prefix}}Sprint Tasks" with a label called "{{prefix}}urgent". Create 5 tasks in that project, each tagged with the "{{prefix}}urgent" label and due next Friday.
